chapter: Childhood and first music in Oklahoma
title: Muskogee carnival job and back to the trumpet
summary: His older brother in Muskogee taught him a few tunes for a carnival job; he gave up clarinet and learned trumpet on the road.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Yeah. I left Boley and went to Muskogee, Oklahoma.
Oh, about twelve or thirteen, somewhere along there.

Anyway, I went down to my brother's, my older brother's, and I went to his house. And he said, 'Well, look, there's a possibility I might be able to get you a job with a carnival coming up here pretty soon.' I said, 'Well,

okay." I said, "I don't know no music, though." So he said, "Well, I'll teach you what you need to know." So he taught me, like, "Dinah" and "Sweet Sue" and numbers like that, something easy that I could play.
And we went on this carnival, and we went up to...we went back to Bristow. I had learned how to play the trumpet, you know, enough to do the tunes at least.
Yeah. I was back on trumpet, learning.
Oh, I see. I misunderstood. I thought you were still playing the clarinet.
Oh, you gave up the clarinet.
I gave up the clarinet and went back to trumpet. That's where I learned how to play "Sweet Sue" and "Sweet Georgia Brown" and so forth.
